newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI CABINET APPROVES BUDGET CUT, TO DETAIL AUG 19.
newsitem.headline: THAI CABINET APPROVES BUDGET CUT, TO DETAIL AUG 19.

text.p: Thailand's cabinet on Monday approved a broad guideline to cut the 1997/1998 (October- September) government budget by 50-70 billion baht ($1.6-2.3 billion) and would review its details on August 19, deputy government spokesman Amnaj Chanawongse said.
He told Reuters after a weekly cabinet meeting that Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh had ordered government departments and agencies to work on a finalised budget cut plan.

"Prime Minister Chavalit has ordered the budget bureau to coordinate with the finance ministry and the National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB) and other related agencies to slash the budget on government spending for fiscal 1998 by 50-70 billion baht," he said.
After working out details, it would be submitted to a cabinet meeting on August 19, he said.

Government sources said the final figures could not be released as the International Monetary Fund and other potential donors were meeting in Tokyo this week to discuss loans to tide Thailand over its economic crisis.
"The meeting is still going on and the IMF wants to know clearcut measures of the Thai government about how much it could cut government spending," the official said.
Thailand's sharp economic slowdown has reduced its tax revenue, and is giving its government its first budget deficits in a decade this year and in the 1997/1998 fiscal year.
The government said the proposed 1997/1998 budget cut would help Thailand's effort to sustain its earlier balanced, deficit-free budget policy.
